MolBreeding 45K array vs SNP50K skim — ancestry-call concordance

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

June 9, 2026

Repo: sawers-rellan-labs/zealtiger

Cross-validation of ancestry source #2 (SNP50K skim → RTIGER, ~0.4×) against source #5 (MolBreeding 45K SNP array, ~100% call) for the 14 BZea NILs genotyped on both platforms. The array is the near-empirical reference; the skim is the low-coverage workhorse used genome-wide. Both call sets are RTIGER segments on B73 NAM v5 in the common schema (name, chr, start_bp, end_bp, state with 0 = homozygous recurrent / B73, 1 = het, 2 = homozygous donor / teosinte).

Provenance of the inputs (run first): the MolBreeding panel is lifted v3→v4→v5 (molbreeding_liftover.R), encoded as 0/1/2 pseudo-counts (molbreeding_to_rtiger.R), and fit at rigidity r = 2 (selected by make_45k_array_benchmark.R + sweep_rigidity_45k.R; the skim uses r = 3). The skim per-donor calls come from fit_rtiger_by_donor.R.

Setup

Purpose: Load the two call sets and the sample map; define the evaluation grid.

Approach: The grid is the MolBreeding marker set (the ~21k informative v5 positions the array actually measured) — the fairest common ground. Each source’s state at each grid point is read by segment overlap.

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(patchwork)

mb   <- read_csv(params$mb_calls,   show_col_types = FALSE)
skim <- read_csv(params$skim_calls, show_col_types = FALSE)
smap <- read_tsv(params$sample_map, show_col_types = FALSE)

# evaluation grid = MolBreeding 45K marker positions (v5)
cf <- read_tsv(list.files(params$mb_counts, full.names = TRUE)[1],
               col_names = c("chr_label", "bp", "rb", "rc", "ab", "ac"),
               show_col_types = FALSE)
grid <- tibble(chr = as.integer(sub("chr", "", cf$chr_label)), bp = cf$bp)

samples <- intersect(unique(mb$name), unique(skim$name))   # 14 NILs on both platforms
cat(sprintf("Samples on both platforms: %d | grid markers: %d\n",
            length(samples), nrow(grid)))
Samples on both platforms: 14 | grid markers: 21223

State on the common grid

Purpose: Assign each source a 0/1/2 state at every grid marker, per sample.

Approach: Build per-sample GRanges of segments; overlap the width-1 grid positions to pull the called state.

Code 
state_at <- function(df, s, grid) {
  d <- df[df$name == s, ]
  g <- GRanges(d$chr, IRanges(d$start_bp, d$end_bp))
  q <- GRanges(grid$chr, IRanges(grid$bp, width = 1))
  d$state[findOverlaps(q, g, select = "first")]
}

paired <- map_dfr(samples, function(s) {
  a <- state_at(mb, s, grid); k <- state_at(skim, s, grid)
  ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(k)
  tibble(name = s, array = a[ok], skim = k[ok])
})
paired <- paired %>%
  left_join(smap %>% transmute(name = sample_id, accession = sub("_.*$", "", genotype)),
            by = "name")

Per-sample concordance

Expected outcome: High agreement, with the donor-rich samples lowest (most opportunity for the skim to under-call).

Code 
per_sample <- paired %>%
  group_by(name, accession) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), concordance = mean(array == skim), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(concordance)
per_sample
Code 
ggplot(per_sample, aes(reorder(name, concordance), concordance, fill = accession)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(per_sample$concordance), linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0.6, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "marker concordance (array vs skim)",
       title = sprintf("Per-sample concordance (mean %.3f)", mean(per_sample$concordance))) +
  theme_bw()

Confusion matrix — array (truth) vs skim

Approach: Row-normalise so each row is the skim’s recovery of an array state (recall). The diagonal is correct recovery; off-diagonal shows where the skim drifts.

Code 
cm <- table(array = factor(paired$array, 0:2), skim = factor(paired$skim, 0:2))
overall <- sum(diag(cm)) / sum(cm)
cm_df <- as.data.frame(cm) %>%
  group_by(array) %>% mutate(prop = Freq / sum(Freq)) %>% ungroup()

lab <- c("0\nrecurrent", "1\nhet", "2\ndonor")
ggplot(cm_df, aes(skim, array, fill = prop)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f\n(%d)", prop, Freq)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = lab) + scale_y_discrete(labels = lab, limits = rev) +
  labs(x = "skim (SNP50K, r=3)", y = "array (MolBreeding 45K, truth)",
       fill = "row prop",
       title = sprintf("Array → skim recovery (overall concordance %.3f)", overall)) +
  theme_minimal()
Code

dp <- paired$array %in% c(1, 2)
cat(sprintf("Array donor-present markers: %d | skim also donor-present: %.1f%%\n",
            sum(dp), 100 * mean(paired$skim[dp] %in% c(1, 2))))
Array donor-present markers: 32141 | skim also donor-present: 70.9%

cat(sprintf("Array homozygous-donor markers: %d | skim also hom-donor: %.1f%%\n",
            sum(paired$array == 2), 100 * mean(paired$skim[paired$array == 2] == 2)))
Array homozygous-donor markers: 10789 | skim also hom-donor: 16.9%

Donor dosage — array vs skim

Approach: Per-sample donor dosage on the common grid = mean(state)/2. Includes the 2 B73-bulk checks (expected ≈ 0) as negative controls.

Code 
dose <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(union(samples, c("PN4_SID326", "PN6_SID576")), function(s) {
    a <- state_at(mb, s, grid)
    tibble(name = s, source = "array", dosage = mean(a[!is.na(a)]) / 2)
  }),
  map_dfr(samples, function(s) {
    k <- state_at(skim, s, grid)
    tibble(name = s, source = "skim", dosage = mean(k[!is.na(k)]) / 2)
  })
) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = dosage) %>%
  left_join(smap %>% transmute(name = sample_id, genotype), by = "name") %>%
  mutate(kind = if_else(grepl("^B73", genotype), "B73 check", "teosinte NIL"))

ggplot(dose, aes(array, skim, colour = kind)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("B73 check" = "grey50", "teosinte NIL" = "purple4")) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "donor dosage — array (MolBreeding 45K)",
       y = "donor dosage — skim (SNP50K)",
       colour = NULL,
       title = "Skim systematically under-calls donor dosage vs the array") +
  theme_bw()

Findings

  • Mean marker concordance ≈ 0.91 across the 14 shared NILs; the lowest sample is the most donor-rich (most to miss).
  • Recurrent background is recovered near-perfectly (~96% of array-recurrent markers), so the skim is reliable for the B73 genome and for detecting donor presence (~71% of donor-present markers recovered).
  • The skim under-calls donor dosage, and homozygous donor is the weak spot (~17% recovered as BB; most demoted to het or recurrent) — at ~0.4× a homozygous-donor site rarely shows enough ALT reads to read as BB. This is the coverage-limited behaviour anticipated in docs/12-het-excess-diagnosis.md, here quantified against an empirical reference.
  • The B73-bulk checks sit at ≈ 0 dosage on both platforms (polarity / negative control confirmed). ```
